items.title: merge_commit_msg.py squash mode
items.action: Wave 1, parallel2 implement lane task-3 (own worktree). Copy the planned files tests/skills/test_merge_commit_msg_squash.py first. In the driver: (a) _parser: capture and build take `--squash`/`-s` (store_true) and an optional positional `mode` (nargs='?', no choices); main normalizes args.squash = flag or mode == 'squash'; any other mode is `problem: unknown mode 'X'; the only mode is squash (--squash, -s)` with exit 1 (D5). (b) subject_line(pr, title, squash=False) returns f'{title} (#{pr})' in squash mode. (c) title_problem gains squash=False: in squash mode a title whose subject_parts type is None or summary empty is `PR #N title 'X' is not a Conventional-Commit subject (Type(scope): summary), which a squash commit needs; retitle it with gh pr edit N --title`. pr_view passes the flag. (d) message_template/render take squash: the subject follows the mode; the facts gain '- Mode: merge' or '- Mode: squash' after Title in both modes (D3); in squash mode only, the heading is '# PR #N squash message' and the instruction names `build --squash`. (e) build: with the flag, line 1 must equal the squash subject; a line 1 equal to the merge subject is `subject is the merge form; drop --squash to keep it, or use '<squash>'`. Without the flag, a line 1 equal to the squash subject switches to squash mode (title check included); otherwise the unchanged merge check and text (D4). (f) receipt says 'squash message' or 'merge message'. Module docstring: both modes, usage lines. No-mode capture output equals GOLDEN in the squash test file (base output plus '- Mode: merge'); the no-mode TXT and receipt stay identical (tests/skills/test_merge_commit_msg.py). Functions under 50 lines; Optional/Union typing.
